method: Every listed verse inspected after source-based drafting. Shared names, counts, short formulas and clear wording retained where appropriate. No quota; this is not independent review or proof of originality.

rows.rationale: Preserves the distinct divine wording and the possible attachment of the final Jerusalem phrase in a note.
rows.before: Whoever is among you of all his people, may his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and rebuild the house of the LORD, the God of Israel—he is the God who is in Jerusalem.
rows.after: Whoever among you belongs to his people—may his God be with him! Let him go up to Jerusalem in Judah and rebuild the house of the LORD, the God of Israel. He is the God who is in Jerusalem.
rows.tsw_comparator: Whoever is among you of all his people, may his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and rebuild the house of the LORD, the God of Israel—he is the God who is in Jerusalem.

rows.rationale: Keeps the former kings’ power and the repeated three revenue categories.
rows.before: Powerful kings have ruled over Jerusalem and governed all the province Beyond the River, and tribute, tax, and toll were paid to them.
rows.after: Powerful kings have ruled Jerusalem and governed all Beyond the River. Tribute, tax, and toll were paid to them.
rows.tsw_comparator: Powerful kings have ruled over Jerusalem and governed all the province Beyond the River, and tribute, tax, and toll were paid to them.

rows.rationale: Preserves the king’s stated interest and the language of pleasing offerings.
rows.before: so that they may offer pleasing sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons.
rows.after: so they may offer pleasing sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the lives of the king and his sons.
rows.tsw_comparator: so that they may offer pleasing sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons.

rows.rationale: Marks the return to Hebrew without changing its concise date statement.
rows.before: The returned exiles kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
rows.after: The returned exiles observed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
rows.tsw_comparator: The returned exiles kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.

rows.rationale: Retains the royal title and marks the Aramaic document opening; the elliptical greeting is noted.
rows.before: “Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, scribe of the instruction of the God of heaven, complete peace. And now:
rows.after: “Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, scribe of the law of the God of heaven: Complete greetings. And now:
rows.tsw_comparator: “Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, scribe of the instruction of the God of heaven, complete peace. And now:

rows.rationale: Keeps the separate bowl value, bronze count, and comparison of value.
rows.before: twenty gold bowls worth one thousand darics, and two vessels of fine gleaming bronze, precious as gold.
rows.after: twenty gold bowls worth a thousand darics, and two vessels of fine, gleaming bronze, as precious as gold.
rows.tsw_comparator: twenty gold bowls worth one thousand darics, and two vessels of fine gleaming bronze, precious as gold.

rows.rationale: Preserves holiness applied both to people and vessels and the voluntary nature of the metals.
rows.before: I said to them, “You are holy to the LORD, and the vessels are holy. The silver and gold are a freewill offering to the LORD, the God of your ancestors.
rows.after: I told them, “You are holy to the LORD, and the vessels are holy. The silver and gold are a voluntary offering to the LORD, the God of your ancestors.
rows.tsw_comparator: I said to them, “You are holy to the LORD, and the vessels are holy. The silver and gold are a freewill offering to the LORD, the God of your ancestors.

rows.rationale: Preserves every number and the source’s final comprehensive burnt-offering statement despite the preceding sin-offering category.
rows.before: The returned exiles who had come from captivity offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering. All of these were a burnt offering to the LORD.
rows.after: The exiles who had returned from captivity offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering. All of it was a burnt offering to the LORD.
rows.tsw_comparator: The returned exiles who had come from captivity offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering. All of these were a burnt offering to the LORD.

rows.rationale: Preserves Ezra’s bodily distress and the two garments without softening self-inflicted pain.
rows.before: When I heard this matter, I tore my garment and my robe, pulled hair from my head and beard, and sat appalled.
rows.after: When I heard this, I tore my garment and robe, pulled hair from my head and beard, and sat appalled.
rows.tsw_comparator: When I heard this matter, I tore my garment and my robe, pulled hair from my head and beard, and sat appalled.

rows.rationale: Keeps both marriage directions, the severe prohibition, and the stated inheritance purpose without softening their scope.
rows.before: So do not give your daughters to their sons, and do not take their daughters for your sons. Never seek their peace or their prosperity, so that you may be strong and eat the good of the land and leave it as an inheritance to your children forever.’
rows.after: Do not give your daughters to their sons or take their daughters for your sons. Never seek their peace or prosperity, so that you may be strong, eat the good of the land, and leave it as an inheritance to your sons forever.’
rows.tsw_comparator: Therefore do not give your daughters to their sons, and do not take their daughters for your sons. Never seek their peace or their prosperity, so that you may be strong and eat the good of the land and leave it as an inheritance to your children forever.’

rows.rationale: Keeps the completion date and administrative scope without adding an account of every wife’s departure.
rows.before: By the first day of the first month they had finished with all the men who had married foreign women.
rows.after: By the first day of the first month, they had finished dealing with all the men who had married foreign women.
rows.tsw_comparator: By the first day of the first month they had finished with all the men who had married foreign women.

rows.rationale: Retains all five names without conflating them with namesakes elsewhere.
rows.before: From the descendants of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
rows.after: From the family of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
rows.tsw_comparator: From the descendants of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.

rows.rationale: Preserves all six names and their order.
rows.before: From the descendants of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
rows.after: From the family of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
rows.tsw_comparator: From the descendants of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.

rows.rationale: Keeps the two service groups distinct and all four names.
rows.before: From the singers: Eliashib. From the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
rows.after: From the singers: Eliashib. From the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
rows.tsw_comparator: From the singers: Eliashib. From the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.

rows.rationale: Retains all six family members and their source order.
rows.before: From the descendants of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah.
rows.after: From the family of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah.
rows.tsw_comparator: From the descendants of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah.

rows.rationale: Preserves the complete six-name Zattu group.
rows.before: From the descendants of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.
rows.after: From the family of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.
rows.tsw_comparator: From the descendants of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.

rows.rationale: Keeps each of the four names distinct from similar names elsewhere.
rows.before: From the descendants of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.
rows.after: From the family of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.
rows.tsw_comparator: From the descendants of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.

rows.rationale: Preserves the eight-name group without abbreviating recurring names.
rows.before: From the descendants of Pahath-Moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh.
rows.after: From the family of Pahath-moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh.
rows.tsw_comparator: From the descendants of Pahath-Moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh.

rows.rationale: Retains the first five names of a list continuing over the verse boundary.
rows.before: From the descendants of Harim: Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,
rows.after: From the family of Harim: Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,

rows.rationale: Completes the Harim group with all three remaining names.
rows.before: Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah.
rows.after: Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah.
rows.tsw_comparator: Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah.

rows.rationale: Keeps the two similar initial names distinct and preserves all seven.
rows.before: From the descendants of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.
rows.after: From the family of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.
rows.tsw_comparator: From the descendants of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.

rows.rationale: Closes the continuing list with all final names intact.
rows.before: Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph.
rows.after: Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph.
rows.tsw_comparator: Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph.
